issues.problem: The opacity reset uses the textbook Mip-Splatting formula logit(min(sigma(o)*coef, 0.01)/coef), with coef taken from the RAW scales. The official WildGaussians code is different. GaussianModel.reset_opacity takes gaussians['scales'] from get_gaussians(), and those scales are ALREADY 3D-filtered (sqrt(s^2+f^2)). It then adds filter_3D^2 a second time, so it divides by coef' = sqrt(prod(s^2+f^2)/prod(s^2+2f^2)) > coef. Result: Gaussians at or below the filter size come out of each reset with filtered opacity well under 0.01. About 0.0065 when s=f. Sub-filter Gaussians (s<<f) get a raw opacity of about sigma(o)*coef/0.35 and are pruned (<0.005) at the next densify. The port instead leaves sub-filter Gaussians untouched, because the ceiling 0.01/coef > 1. Every reset is affected: 3000/6000/9000/12000 for On-the-go and every 15000 up to 100k for Photo Tourism. This changes which Gaussians survive, and the plan says the code is followed.
issues.evidence: source/code/wildgaussians/method.py:1249-1266 (scales = gaussians['scales'] -> filtered; scales_after_square = scales_square + filter_3D^2) vs method.py:1060-1078 (get_gaussians returns filtered scales) vs geometry.py:361-365 (coef from raw log_scales). Probe filter_3d (probes.py:388-395) checks the plugin's own formula, filtered opacity == min(old, 0.01), so it encodes the non-official reference.
issues.fix: Port the official formula: f_op = sigmoid(o)*coef(raw); new_raw = min(f_op, 0.01) / sqrt(prod(s_f^2)/prod(s_f^2+f^2)), with s_f = sqrt(s^2+f^2); logit; and log-space for underflow. Update the filter-3d probe to the official reference and list it as an official quirk in paper.md section 7.

issues.problem: Abs-gradient statistic is ||(sum|gx|, sum|gy|)||_2; official GOF rasterizer accumulates the scalar sum_pixels(|gx|+|gy|) (L1) in channel z and takes norm of that single channel.
issues.fix: a = (absgrad0+absgrad1)*scale; stats['abs'] += a[vis].sum(-1). Rank-based quantile makes the effect small, but it is a one-line fix.

issues.problem: gsplat 1.5.3 culls Gaussians whose (filtered, compensated) opacity < 1/255 (radii 0) and uses an opacity-aware extent <= 3.33 sigma. The official rasterizer counts them as visible (radius 3 sigma), so denom differs for faint/sub-filter Gaussians. The alpha cap is also 0.999 vs 0.99. Otherwise antialiased + eps2d 0.1 is the same Mip 2D filter (cov+0.1 I, sqrt(det0/det1) compensation). This is an adequate stand-in.
issues.fix: Record the opacity-aware culling in the fidelity-gap list; optionally set alpha_cap 0.99.

issues.problem: The report omits the reset-formula difference, the L1/L2 abs-grad difference, gsplat opacity-aware culling, and the fact that the Gaussian Adam step on densify/reset iterations is skipped in the official code (new nn.Parameters have no grad) but not in the port.

The On-the-go paper-vs-code conflict is unresolved. Paper Tab. 4 'Ours' high (23.03) equals the Tab. 7 patio-high/spot mean and differs from 'w/o app.' (22.80), so appearance-on is the right headline. But the released nerfonthego.yml / HF checkpoints are appearance-off. Running noapp only optionally leaves this open.
issues.fix: Run wildgaussians-noapp on the same scenes as a required second row.

issues.problem: The smoke comparison (20.60 vs gsplat 20.82 at 2k steps) mixes protocols: gsplat uses white bg and ss-eval LPIPS-VGG, while WG uses black bg and NerfBaselines uint8/dm_pix/LPIPS-Alex. Masking only starts at step 2000. It is a path check only and says nothing about the improvement.
issues.fix: Evaluate the gsplat baseline with the same official_metrics (uint8, dm_pix, LPIPS-Alex) when comparing the improvement against the paper's +4.94/+3.96 over 3DGS.

summary: The port is faithful to the official code almost everywhere. The appearance MLP, Fourier init and DINO uncertainty loss/mask match the extracted official classes numerically: MLP and Fourier diff 0, uncertainty loss equal in train and eval mode, mask agreement 100%. The loss split, the warm-up and protected windows, the hyper-parameters and LRs (head 1e-3, Adam eps 1e-15, BN train / eval at test time), the SH schedule, the two-pass renderer with per-Gaussian SH toning, the NeRF-W protocol, NerfBaselines metrics and data/splits are all correct. gsplat antialiased with eps2d 0.1 is an adequate Mip 2D-filter stand-in. Appearance-on is the right On-the-go headline, because Tab. 4 'Ours' high 23.03 equals the Tab. 7 patio-high/spot mean. One major deviation: the filter-aware opacity reset follows Mip-Splatting rather than WildGaussians' double-filtered formula, and that changes which Gaussians survive every reset. Plus minor abs-grad-norm and reporting issues. Pytest 12/12 passed and ss-inspect reports no issues.
